newsitem.title: USA: World Bank plans $160 million for Bosnia in 1997.
newsitem.headline: World Bank plans $160 million for Bosnia in 1997.

text.p: The World Bank plans to approve some $160 million in low-cost loans for Bosnia this year as part of an expected $1.4 billion global programme to help rebuild the war-torn nation in 1997, officials said on Friday.

Christine Wallich, Director for Bosnia at the Bank, told reporters that it would focus much of its effort this year on promoting economic reforms, including privatisation in the banking and other sectors.

The World Bank and more than 60 other donors are scheduled to meet in Brussels next week to map out guidelines for their financing programme for Bosnia in 1997. A pledging session is expected in early March.
In 1996, donor nations and international organisations pledged $1.8 billion for reconstruction of Bosnia. The World Bank share was $330 million.
Wallich argued that the foreign financing has made a difference, but acknowledged that much more needed to be done to put Bosnia's war-shattered economy back together.
"The results really have been quite extraordinary," she said. But she added: "We still have a very, very difficult situation."

The vast bulk of the foreign assistance for Bosnia has gone to the Moslem-Croat Federation. Bosnia's Serb republic has received only $24 million, in part because of an international embargo that has since been lifted.
The expected 1997 financing programme of $1.4 billion assumes some "catch-up" of assistance to the Serb republic.

Wallich said donors generally agreed that more money should go to the republic, on condition on its making progress in living up to the terms of the Dayton peace agreement that ended 43 months of strife in late 1995.

The European Commission, which is coordinating the reconstruction programme for Bosnia together with the World Bank, plans to focus its efforts this year on fostering the return of refugees from the war, many of whom are in Europe.
"The return of refugees has significantly fallen short of expectations," the World Bank and the EC said in a joint report prepared for the Brussels donor meeting on Jan. 9-10.
According to the report, Bosnia will need some $310 million for its energy sector this year, $180 million for industry and finance, $175 million for transportation and $150 million for housing.
